2403.19817.methods: The authors construct a specific open set of small measure where any finite collection of non-monotonic selection strategies fails to exceed a predetermined capital threshold when evaluated on sequences within that set.
2403.19817.regime: The result applies to computable, non-monotonic betting strategies (Kolmogorov-Loveland strategies) operating on infinite binary sequences with respect to the uniform Lebesgue measure.

2403.15871.problem: The paper analyzes the computational complexity and approximability of finding a minimum-size string partition where the dependency chain required to resolve any character's reference is bounded by a constant.
2403.15871.methods: The authors employ complexity-theoretic reductions from hard decision problems to establish NP-hardness and inapproximability bounds for constrained string factorization.
2403.15871.regime: The results apply to the theoretical worst-case complexity of string compression algorithms under strict, constant-bounded random access constraints.
2403.15871.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that enforcing strict local-decodability constraints on dictionary-based compression schemes generally introduces NP-hardness and rules out polynomial-time approximation schemes.

2404.00812.problem: The paper investigates whether there exists a single, universal problem to which all other problems with constant-cost randomized communication complexity can be reduced.
2404.00812.methods: The authors employ communication complexity reductions and structural analysis of randomized protocols to analyze the relationships between constant-cost communication problems.
2404.00812.regime: The result applies to the regime of randomized communication complexity with public coins, specifically focusing on protocols with constant communication cost.
2404.00812.hypothesized_generalization: The result suggests that constant-cost randomized communication complexity does not possess a natural complete problem, hinting at a structural divergence from other complexity classes that admit complete problems.

2404.00006.problem: The paper evaluates the correctness and computational complexity of a proposed polynomial-time algorithm for a known NP-complete decision problem that determines if a boolean formula in 2-conjunctive normal form has an assignment satisfying at least a target number of clauses.
2404.00006.methods: The authors construct counterexamples to demonstrate algorithmic failure and analyze the runtime complexity of operations on boolean formulas transformed between conjunctive and disjunctive normal forms.
2404.00006.regime: The analysis applies to worst-case instances of NP-complete decision problems under asymptotic polynomial-time bounds.
2404.00006.hypotheses_generalization: The failure of the proposed algorithm supports the widely held complexity-theoretic hypothesis that P is not equal to NP.

2403.19911.problem: The paper addresses the problem of finding an approximate fixed point of a contraction map over the multi-dimensional unit cube under the infinity norm using a polynomial number of queries to the map.
2403.19911.methods: The authors employ a black-box reduction to reduce the contraction parameter to a constant, combined with a recursive binary search procedure over the coordinate dimensions of the map.
2403.19911.regime: The result applies to the query complexity regime where both the approximation parameter and the contraction parameter are inversely exponential in the input dimension, and the algorithm accesses the map solely through an oracle.
2403.19911.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that finding approximate fixed points for non-expansive maps under the infinity norm is computationally tractable in polynomial queries, whereas finding strong approximations to the exact fixed point of such non-expansive maps is fundamentally impossible.

2404.01080.problem: Determining the computational complexity boundary between tractable and intractable cases for a class of constraint satisfaction problems over finite domains.
2404.01080.methods: Constructing a hierarchical sequence of subuniverses and equivalence relations to unify local algebraic structures with global connectivity properties.
2404.01080.regime: Finite constraint languages preserved by a weak near-unanimity operation.
2404.01080.hyporhesized_generalization: The algebraic decomposition techniques could extend to characterizing the complexity of constraint satisfaction problems over infinite domains with similar symmetry conditions.

2404.02912.problem: The paper investigates the exact relationship, in terms of representation and tractability, between probabilistic generating circuits and standard probabilistic circuits that allow negative edge weights.
2404.02912.methods: The authors construct structural transformations between arithmetic circuits computing probability generating functions and those computing probability mass functions, analyzing the semantic properties of set-multilinear polynomials.
2404.02912.regime: The theoretical analysis applies to tractable probabilistic models representing discrete probability distributions, specifically comparing binary and multi-categorical variable settings.
2404.02912.hypothesized_generalization: The equivalence suggests that the tractability of complex probabilistic models is determined by semantic constraints on the computed polynomials rather than the specific syntactic representation of the circuit.

2404.03774.problem: The paper investigates whether active data collection and exploration are fundamentally more computationally difficult than passive prediction when learning unknown dynamical systems.
2404.03774.methods: The authors construct cryptographic hardness reductions that map hard-to-invert one-way functions to the task of policy optimization in reinforcement learning.
2404.03774.regime: The results apply to the polynomial-time computational complexity regime, establishing a formal separation between reinforcement learning and supervised learning under standard cryptographic assumptions.
2404.03774.hypothesized_generalization: The computational bottleneck in complex decision-making tasks is inherently driven by the active search for informative states rather than the representation learning of observed data.

2404.03812.problem: The paper studies the problem of finding a minimum-cardinality set of isometric paths in a graph such that the maximum distance from any vertex to its nearest path is minimized.
2404.03812.methods: The authors use a novel shallow pairing property to merge a set of rooted isometric paths sharing a common endpoint into a smaller set of unrooted isometric paths, operating on metric spaces with bounded delta-hyperbolicity.
2404.03812.range_of_applicability: The results apply to delta-hyperbolic graphs of arbitrary size, providing a polynomial-time additive approximation algorithm with an error bound depending only on the hyperbolicity parameter.
2404.03812.hypothesized_generalization: The shallow pairing property of delta-hyperbolic graphs may generalize to other metric spaces with bounded tree-like structures, enabling additive approximations for other facility location and path-covering problems.

2404.03844.problem: The paper classifies the computational complexity of the Quantified Constraint Satisfaction Problem (QCSP) over finite domains, specifically establishing a dichotomy between the complexity class $\Pi_{2}^{P}$ and PSpace-completeness.
2404.03844.methods: The approach uses algebraic reductions and structural analysis of constraint languages to bound the size of universal variable subsets required to determine the outcome of a quantified game.
2404.03844.regime: The results apply to quantified decision problems defined over finite domains with arbitrary constraint languages.
2404.03844.hypothesized_generalization: The dichotomy suggests that the complexity of quantified satisfaction problems is fundamentally constrained by the size of the minimal winning strategies for the universal player, hinting at a broader classification of polynomial-space problems based on strategy size.

2404.04395.problem: The paper identifies a logical flaw in a proposed polynomial-time algorithm for an NP-complete decision problem, specifically showing that the algorithm incorrectly classifies certain satisfiable instances as unsatisfiable.
2404.04395.methods: The authors construct a concrete counterexample to analyze the propagation of constraints and contradiction pairs within a layered tree-like representation of boolean formulas.
2404.04395.regime: The analysis applies to the theoretical verification of computational complexity claims, specifically the P versus NP question in discrete mathematics and theoretical computer science.
2404.04395.hypothesized_generalization: The result reinforces the consensus that simple iterative constraint-propagation heuristics are insufficient to solve NP-complete problems in polynomial time.

2404.04504.problem: Determining whether a set of rectangular tiles with colored edges can tile the infinite plane under edge-matching constraints when the number of available tile types is restricted to a small, fixed constant.
2404.04504.methods: Constructing a reduction from the classical undecidable Wang domino problem using a simplified framework of a fixed number of Wang bars that encodes tile selection and alignment without requiring a distinct jaw-like containment structure.
2404.04504.regime: The theoretical limit of undecidability for plane-tiling problems, specifically establishing undecidability for a small, fixed number of Wang bars (exactly 11) and consequently for Wang tiles with a low, fixed color deficiency.
2404.04504.hypothesized_generalization: The boundary between decidability and undecidability for 2D tiling problems can be pushed to extremely small, fixed parameter bounds by optimizing the geometric and color-matching encoding mechanisms.

2404.04705.problem: The paper solves the twisted conjugacy problem for even dihedral Artin groups, which are isomorphic to the Baumslag-Solitar groups BS(n, n).
2404.04705.methods: The authors construct a decision algorithm by analyzing word relations and minimal-length representatives under a semidirect product decomposition, showing that minimal-length twisted conjugate elements are related by a finite sequence of shift operations.
2404.04705.regime: The results apply to all outer automorphisms of even dihedral Artin groups, establishing quadratic time complexity for the decision algorithm and proving orbit decidability for all finitely generated subgroups of their automorphism groups.
2404.04705.hypothesized_generalization: The solvability of the twisted conjugacy problem for these groups suggests that similar semidirect product decompositions and rewriting systems can resolve decision problems in wider classes of Baumslag-Solitar groups and their extensions.

2404.06427.problem: The paper constructs explicit, universal sequences of tensors that exactly characterize the worst-case tensor exponent in a primal space, providing a concrete mechanism to resolve Strassen's asymptotic rank conjecture.
2404.06427.methods: The authors construct zero-one-valued tensor sequences via diagonalization and relate the absence of low-degree polynomials vanishing on low-rank tensors to upper bounds on the tensor exponent.
2404.06427.regime: The results apply to the asymptotic regime of tensor Kronecker powers over infinite fields, specifically characterizing the worst-case exponents of tensors of a given format.
2404.06427.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint that the asymptotic rank of any tensor space can be tightly bounded and characterized by a single, explicitly constructible universal sequence of combinatorial tensors.

2404.06720.problem: The paper establishes the optimal tradeoff between query complexity and memory capacity for finding a point within a target region using a separation oracle.
2404.06720.methods: The analysis uses information-theoretic lower bounds to constrain the performance of deterministic and randomized query algorithms operating on high-dimensional convex sets.
2404.06720.regime: The results apply to high-dimensional feasibility problems where the memory capacity ranges from linear to quadratic in the dimension, and the target accuracy is arbitrarily small.
2404.06720.hypothesized_generalization: The sharp phase transition at quadratic memory suggests that a fundamental computational barrier prevents sub-quadratic memory algorithms from achieving sub-polynomial query complexity in high-dimensional search and optimization problems.

2404.07037.problem: The paper addresses the computational complexity of finding the canonical direct-like representation (specifically the D-base) and its underlying dependency relation (the D-relation) of a finite closure system from alternative representations like implicational bases or meet-irreducible elements.
2404.07037.methods: The authors design output-quasi-polynomial and polynomial-delay algorithms, alongside proving NP-completeness, to characterize the complexity of translating between different representations of closure systems.
2404.07037.regime: The results apply to finite closure systems, finite lattices, and propositional Horn formulas of arbitrary size.
2404.07037.hypothesized_generalization: The tractability of computing minimal generators under binary-implication minimality suggests that other structural bases of closure systems can be efficiently computed by exploiting localized dependency relations.

2404.07288.problem: This paper investigates the relationship between computational universality and dynamical complexity by determining whether Turing complete dynamical systems must exhibit positive topological entropy.
2404.07288.methods: The authors define a computable regularity criterion for Turing machines and analyze the topological entropy of their symbolic dynamics and continuous embeddings using topological dynamics and Cantor set constructions.
2404.07288.regime: The results apply to discrete-time symbolic dynamical systems representing Turing machines, as well as continuous-time area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk and stationary 3D Euler fluid flows.
2404.07288.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that physical systems capable of universal computation generally require chaotic dynamics with positive topological entropy, unless the simulation encodings are highly irregular.

2404.07606.problem: Bounding the communication complexity of a composed function in terms of the query complexity of the outer function and the communication complexity of the inner function.
2404.07606.methods: Lifting theorems that analyze the discrepancy of the inner function, operating on combinatorial rectangles and query-to-communication simulation protocols.
2404.07606.regime: Every pair of functions where the inner function has a discrepancy that is at most inverse polynomial in its input length.
2404.07606.hypothesized_generalization: Lifting theorems may hold for a much broader class of complex inner functions beyond those with exponentially small discrepancy, potentially leading to a unified direct-sum theory for communication complexity.

2404.07881.problem: The paper analyzes the asymptotic behavior and dynamics of high-dimensional iterative algorithms that alternate linear matrix multiplications with coordinate-wise non-linearities under random matrix inputs.
2404.07881.methods: The authors analyze these algorithms by mapping their operations to combinatorial operations on a diagrammatic basis derived from a symmetry-reduced Fourier basis, reducing the analysis to counting self-avoiding tree-like graphs.
2404.07881.regime: The results rigorously apply to first-order iterations running for a constant number of steps, with extensions to power iteration where the number of iterations scales up to the square root of the matrix dimension.
2404.07881.hypothesized_generalization: The authors conjecture that the tree diagram representation and its corresponding Gaussian approximation can be extended to describe the dynamics of power iteration up to a linear number of iterations in the matrix dimension, but no further.

2404.07801.problem: The paper addresses the problem of uniquely decomposing a three-way array into a sum of a minimal number of outer products of vectors, specifically in cases where the number of terms exceeds the dimensions of the array.
2404.07801.methods: The proposed approach uses commuting matrix extensions and diagonalization of slice matrices to reconstruct the constituent vectors of the decomposition.
2404.07801.regime: The results apply to third-order tensors of size $n \times n \times n$ where the rank $r$ is strictly less than $n^2/4$, operating in polynomial time with respect to the input size.
2404.07801.hypothesized_generalization: The algebraic conditions used to guarantee uniqueness and efficient recovery suggest that similar commuting matrix extension techniques could be generalized to decompose higher-order tensors of even larger rank.

2404.07986.problem: The paper addresses the problem of deterministically deciding the invertibility and computing the rank of a matrix whose entries are linear forms over a partially commutative polynomial ring.
2404.07986.methods: The authors design a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm by reducing the algebraic equivalence problem of multi-tape weighted automata to identity testing of partially commutative algebraic branching programs, utilizing cyclic division algebras and a constructive regularity lemma.
2404.07986.regime: The result applies to the setting where the number of partitioned variable sets is a constant, operating over a skew field of fractions of a partially commutative polynomial ring in characteristic zero.
2404.07986.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest a broader trade-off between variable noncommutativity and the complexity of polynomial identity testing, hinting that deterministic tractability can be maintained when interpolating between fully commutative and fully noncommutative algebraic structures.

2404.08158.problem: The paper addresses the problem of verifying the correctness of an agnostically learned hypothesis using significantly fewer data samples and computational resources than required to learn the hypothesis from scratch.
2404.08158.methods: The authors construct interactive proof protocols that leverage Fourier analysis of Boolean functions, tolerant natural properties, and transformations from membership queries to random examples.
2404.08158.regime: The results apply to the uniform distribution setting for learning heavy Fourier characters, Boolean circuit classes, and juntas, using sample complexities that are quasi-polynomial or independent of the input dimension.
2404.08158.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that interactive verification can bypass classical sample complexity lower bounds for hard learning problems, potentially extending to broader classes of distribution-free learning.

2404.08870.problem: Establishing tight computational time lower bounds for approximating NP-hard parameterized optimization problems, specifically finding approximate cliques in graphs and satisfying assignments for constraint satisfaction problems.
2404.08870.methods: The paper constructs a parallel probabilistically checkable proof of almost linear size by applying Reed-Muller error-correcting codes and derandomized low-degree polynomial testing to a vector-structured constraint satisfaction problem.
2404.08870.regime: The results apply to the parameterized complexity regime under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, where the parameter is a super-constant much smaller than the input size.
2404.08870.thought_process: The paper hints at a general framework where the optimal time complexity of approximating any hard parameterized problem can be tightly characterized by combining parallel PCPs with structured, derandomized algebraic codes.

2404.09798.problem: The paper investigates the fine-grained computational complexity of constraint satisfaction problems restricted to binary symmetric relations, specifically analyzing the relative hardness of graph homomorphism problems.
2404.09798.methods: The authors employ an algebraic approach, analyzing the inclusion structure of partial and total polymorphisms of graphs and characterizing projective cores.
2404.09798.regime: The results apply to finite, simple, undirected, non-bipartite core graphs, with specific verification of the Okrasa and Rzążewski conjecture for graphs with at most 7 vertices.
2404.09798.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that the length of the shortest odd cycle in a graph serves as a fundamental parameter determining the fine-grained complexity of its corresponding homomorphism problem.

2404.09236.problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of determining graph parameters related to vertex infection processes under cycle convexity, specifically focusing on the interval number, hull number, rank, and convexity number.
2404.09236.methods: The authors analyze the structural properties of induced subgraphs, cycle structures, and vertex neighborhoods to establish complexity bounds and algorithmic hardness results.
2404.09236.regime: The results apply to finite, simple graphs, with specific hardness classifications and bounds derived for bipartite graphs, planar graphs, grids, and regular graphs.
2404.09236.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that graph convexity parameters defined by cycle-based infection rules share deep complexity barriers with classical feedback vertex set and forest-induction problems across general graph classes.

2404.10023.problem: The paper investigates the parameterized complexity of modifying a graph via vertex deletion, edge editing, edge deletion, or edge addition to obtain a disjoint union of equal-sized cliques.
2404.10023.methods: The authors employ kernelization algorithms to reduce the input graph size, producing polynomial and linear kernels based on structural graph theory and bounded-size components.
2404.10023.regime: The results apply to the fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) regime where the parameter is the solution size, representing the maximum number of allowed graph modification operations.
2404.10023.hypothesized_generalization: The polynomial kernelization bounds achieved for uniform cluster graphs suggest that more general balanced cluster editing problems, where component size differences are bounded by a small constant, may also admit significantly improved kernel sizes.

2404.08370.problem: The paper establishes lower bounds on proof size and memory requirements for a propositional proof system that extends resolution with linear equations modulo two.
2404.08370.methods: The authors construct combinatorial Prover-Delayer and Spoiler-Duplicator games to analyze the complexity of extensible formulas, such as the ordering and pigeonhole principles.
2404.08370.regime: The results apply to tree-like refutations and space complexity measures within propositional proof complexity and SAT solving theory.
2404.08370.hypothesized_generalization: The game-theoretic characterizations of size and space complexity may generalize to resolution systems operating over arbitrary rings beyond modulo-two arithmetic.

2404.10670.problem: The paper introduces a new graph width parameter to measure how closely a given graph structurally resembles an interval graph, and evaluates its computational tractability for solving classical NP-hard graph optimization problems.
2404.10670.methods: The authors analyze parameterized complexity and establish tractability boundaries by designing fixed-parameter tractable algorithms and proving hardness results based on the simultaneous interval number combined with solution size.
2404.10670.regime: The results apply to finite, undirected graphs, specifically comparing the parameter's performance against linear mim-width in the context of parameterized complexity classes like FPT and W[1].
2404.10670.hyporhesized_generalization: The parameterization framework suggests that other width measures based on geometric intersection models can be systematically relaxed to yield tractable parameterized algorithms for problems that are otherwise hard under standard width parameters.

2404.10712.problem: Determine the computational complexity of a discrete grid-filling and line-clearing game when the set of available piece types is restricted to size-two subsets.
2404.10712.methods: We use parsimonious reductions from strongly NP-complete partitioning problems to construct board configurations and piece sequences that simulate logical gates and numerical constraints under specific rotation and gravity models.
2404.10712.regime: The theoretical limit of minimal piece variety, specifically analyzing all 21 possible pairs of the seven standard tetromino shapes under the Super Rotation System.
2404.10712.hypothesized_generalization: The hardness of grid-packing games is driven by the spatial interaction of any two distinct asymmetric shapes, suggesting that almost all non-trivial subsets of piece types in similar tiling games are NP-hard.

2404.10839.problem: The paper addresses the parallel complexity of computing fundamental linear and polynomial algebra operations, such as the greatest common divisor, squarefree decomposition, and matrix inversion, using constant-depth arithmetic circuits.
2404.10839.methods: The authors develop new algorithmic techniques to compute symmetric functions of polynomial roots and manipulate root multiplicities without explicitly computing the roots themselves, extending these methods to multivariate polynomials represented by constant-depth circuits.
2404.10839.regime: The results apply to univariate and multivariate polynomials over fields of characteristic zero (or sufficiently large characteristic) in the regime of polynomial-size, constant-depth arithmetic circuits.
2404.10839.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques suggest that a much broader class of algebraic and elimination-theoretic problems, traditionally thought to require sequential processing or high-depth circuits, can be efficiently parallelized into constant depth.

2404.10959.problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity and approximability of computing the permanent of positive semidefinite (PSD) matrices.
2404.10959.methods: The authors employ geometric inapproximability techniques, matrix norm analysis, and reductions from hard constraint satisfaction problems to establish hardness bounds.
2404.10959.regime: The results apply to polynomial-time approximation algorithms for high-dimensional positive semidefinite matrices under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions.
2404.10959.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest a fundamental threshold for the approximability of matrix permanents that may extend to broader classes of structured non-negative matrices.

2404.10961.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of establishing concentration of measure and reverse hypercontractivity properties on high-dimensional expanders to enable optimal agreement testing and property testing.
2404.10961.methods: The authors develop new agreement testing theorems, including a 99%-regime test and a Z-test variant, by analyzing random walks and spectral expansion properties on high-dimensional simplicial complexes.
2404.10961.regime: The results apply to high-dimensional expanders (HDX) under the assumption of strong spectral expansion, specifically achieving optimal soundness and geometric overlap in bounded-degree constructions.
2404.10961.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques suggest that high-dimensional expanders can serve as a general, bounded-degree alternative to complete complexes and product spaces for constructing optimal probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and error-correcting codes.

2404.11096.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing unknown formal languages or state-transition systems from queries and counterexamples within polynomial time limits.
2404.11096.methods: The work analyzes and compares exact learning algorithms that construct minimal deterministic finite automata by querying an oracle for membership and equivalence.
2404.11096.regime: The analysis applies to the theoretical limit of polynomial time and query complexity in the size of the target automaton and the length of the longest counterexample.
2404.11096.hypothesized_generalization: The systematic comparison of these algorithms suggests a unified framework for learning more complex grammatical structures, such as context-free grammars or infinite-state systems, under similar polynomial constraints.

2404.11389.problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of finding a d-cut, which is a vertex partition where each vertex has at most d neighbors on the opposite side, in graphs restricted by diameter, radius, or forbidden induced subgraphs.
2404.11389.methods: The authors analyze the boundary between polynomial-time solvability and NP-completeness by exploiting structural properties of graphs with bounded distance metrics and forbidden induced subgraphs.
2404.11389.regime: The results apply to finite, connected undirected graphs under structural constraints such as bounded diameter, bounded radius, and H-freeness for fixed integers d.
2404.11389.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest a general complexity dichotomy for the d-cut problem on H-free graphs, mirroring the known classification for the matching cut problem.

2404.11709.problem: The paper characterizes the conditions under which constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) over arbitrary finite domains exhibit a satisfiability gap when evaluated over operator-valued assignments on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
2404.11709.methods: The authors analyze the algebraic structure of CSPs using the framework of polymorphisms and local consistency algorithms to classify the power of non-commutative, operator-valued solutions.
2404.11709.regime: The results apply to constraint satisfaction problems defined over arbitrary finite domains and finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
2404.11709.hypothesized_generalization: The dichotomy between bounded-width and other CSPs suggests a universal boundary for when quantum or operator-valued relaxations can perfectly simulate classical satisfiability.

2405.18439.problem: The paper addresses the question of whether a hierarchical classification of computational complexity classes, defined by nested existential and universal quantifiers, collapses to a finite level.
2405.18439.methods: The approach utilizes structural complexity theory and diagonalizing arguments over resource-bounded computation models to establish separation between successive levels of the hierarchy.
2405.18439.regime: The result applies to the asymptotic limit of worst-case time complexity for decision problems solvable in polynomial time with access to oracles.
2405.18439.hypothesized_generalization: The non-collapse of this hierarchy strongly supports the conjecture that P is not equal to NP and that infinite hierarchies of resource-bounded computations generally do not collapse.

2406.08493.problem: The paper addresses the logical validity of foundational proofs asserting that all formal languages are countable, identifying potential gaps in widely accepted mathematical proofs within set theory and computability.
2406.08493.methods: The author performs a critical logical analysis of the standard proofs of countability, examining the mapping functions between infinite sets and the formal definitions of computability.
2406.08493.regime: The analysis applies to the theoretical foundations of discrete mathematics, set theory, and computability theory, specifically concerning infinite sets and formal language theory.
2406.08493.hypothesized_generalization: The work hints at a potential restructuring of the relationship between countable and computable sets, suggesting that some standard assumptions about the cardinality of formal languages may require formal revision.

2412.11914.problem: The paper aims to determine the maximum number of edges in a graph of a given order that can be embedded in the Euclidean plane such that all adjacent vertices are at a unit distance, and to classify all such maximal graphs.
2412.11914.methods: The authors combine combinatorial graph enumeration and forbidden subgraph filtering with a specialized geometric solver that uses Euclidean geometry and linear algebra to find embeddings or prove non-embeddability.
2412.11914.regime: The results apply to small, finite point sets in the two-dimensional real vector space, specifically providing exact solutions and classifications for graphs with up to 12 vertices.
2412.11914.hyporhesized_generalization: The success of combining combinatorial filtering with specialized geometric solvers suggests that the exact determination of maximum edge densities for unit-distance graphs can be pushed to larger finite vertex sets by systematically identifying minimal forbidden subgraphs and leveraging local geometric constraints.

2502.09176.problem: The paper aims to classify the source-algebra equivalence classes of blocks with cyclic defect groups by determining their associated endo-permutation module invariants.
2502.09176.methods: The authors analyze the character tables of finite groups of Lie type, specifically computing sign sequences of Deligne-Lusztig characters and utilizing Brauer correspondents to reduce classical groups to general linear and unitary cases.
2502.09176.regime: The results apply to cyclic blocks of quasisimple groups of Lie type in characteristic different from the block characteristic, specifically focusing on general linear and unitary groups.
2502.09176.hypothesized_generalization: The reduction techniques and character-theoretic computations suggest a systematic way to classify source-algebra equivalence classes for all blocks with cyclic defect groups across all finite groups.

2502.11080.problem: The paper investigates the boundedness and topological properties of the singular and dicritical loci of foliated structures under positivity and singularity constraints.
2502.11080.methods: The authors analyze algebraic foliations on complete toric varieties by utilizing the combinatorial structure of fans, support functions of torus-invariant divisors, and birational geometry of foliated structures.
2502.11080.regime: The results apply to toric foliations of arbitrary rank on complete, normal toric varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
2502.11080.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that the boundedness of adjoint foliated structures and the connectedness of their singular loci may extend from the toric setting to more general Fano varieties.

2502.11188.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of unifying statistical inference and probability spaces with differential geometry and topological field theory through a shared algebraic framework.
2502.11188.methods: The authors construct connections between statistical manifolds and topological field theories by mapping probability distributions and Amari-Chentsov tensors to the algebraic structures of pre-Frobenius and Frobenius manifolds.
2502.11188.regime: The mathematical framework applies generally to finite-dimensional statistical models, smooth probability manifolds, and their associated category-theoretic representations.
2502.11188.hypothesized_generalization: The synthesis suggests that learning processes and statistical decision rules can be generalized as dynamical flows governed by topological invariants, such as Gromov-Witten invariants, on statistical Frobenius manifolds.

2502.11224.problem: Characterizing the local geometric behavior of a subvariety germ embedded in an ambient space by identifying the minimal support of combinatorial fans that yield proper toric modifications.
2502.11224.methods: Equating valuation-theoretic, arc-theoretic, and toric-geometric constructions to define and analyze local tropicalizations of formal subgerms of affine toric varieties.
2502.11224.regime: Local complex analytic and formal geometry of singular subvarieties embedded in toric varieties, particularly plane curves and splice-type surface singularities.
2502.11224.hypod_generalization: Extending local tropicalization to logarithmic schemes, non-Archimedean analytic spaces, and arbitrary commutative rings not containing a field.

2502.11288.problem: The paper aims to characterize decomposable, principally polarized abelian varieties by the non-surjectivity of certain algebraic maps, establishing an analog to classical characterizations of hyperelliptic curves.
2502.11288.methods: The authors analyze the surjectivity of global section multiplication maps and higher-order Gaussian maps defined on line bundles representing the polarization of abelian varieties.
2502.11288.regime: The results apply to finite-dimensional polarized abelian varieties, with a primary focus on the case of principal polarizations of dimension at least two.
2502.11288.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest a potential generalization of Green-Lazarsfeld's results on projective normality and syzygies of curves to the setting of abelian varieties.

2502.11388.problem: The paper aims to construct and classify families of three-dimensional manifolds equipped with indefinite Einstein-Weyl structures that possess closed, simple spacelike geodesics.
2502.11388.methods: The authors construct compact minitwistor spaces of arbitrary genus by embedding hyperelliptic curves with real structures into projective cones, and analyze the resulting moduli spaces of Lorentzian Einstein-Weyl structures using Jacobian varieties and Abel-Jacobi maps.
2502.11388.regime: The results apply to compact minitwistor spaces of arbitrary genus $g \ge 1$ and their associated three-dimensional Lorentzian Einstein-Weyl manifolds.
2502.11388.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest a broader correspondence between the topology of real algebraic curves and the global geodesic behavior of indefinite Einstein-Weyl structures on associated moduli spaces.

2502.11582.problem: The paper aims to establish the isotriviality of certain families of higher-dimensional algebraic varieties parameterized by complex curves, specifically by bounding the intersection numbers of curves on arithmetic quotients of complex hyperbolic spaces.
2502.11582.methods: The authors employ volume estimation techniques and local geometric analysis near quotient singularities on complex hyperbolic 2-balls, utilizing the Bergman metric and projective unitary group representations.
2502.11582.regime: The results apply to compact arithmetic quotients of the complex hyperbolic 2-ball, specifically focusing on the geometry near 1-dimensional and non-cyclic quotient singularities.
2502.11582.hypothesized_generalization: The volume estimation techniques near quotient singularities could potentially be generalized to higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space quotients to prove similar finiteness or isotriviality results for families of abelian varieties.

2502.11704.problem: The paper aims to compute the motivic distribution and asymptotic behavior of the moduli space of morphisms from a smooth projective curve to a variety, subject to specific boundary tangency conditions.
2502.11704.methods: The authors employ Cox rings, universal torsors, and motivic Euler products to parameterize and decompose the classes of these moduli spaces within the Grothendieck ring of varieties.
2502.11704.regime: The results apply to morphisms from arbitrary smooth projective curves to Mori Dream Spaces, with explicit applications to smooth split projective toric varieties over an arbitrary base field.
2502.11704.hypothesized_generalization: The algebraic parameterization via universal torsors suggests that the motivic Batyrev-Manin-Peyre principle can be extended to describe the distribution of rational curves on more general classes of varieties with boundary conditions.

2502.11790.problem: The paper establishes a geometric and algebraic equivalence between resolutions of singularities for Schubert varieties and the moduli spaces of subrepresentations of a quiver.
2502.11790.methods: The authors construct a specific rigid representation of a grid-like quiver with relations and define explicit isomorphisms between its quiver Grassmannians and Bott-Samelson varieties.
2502.11790.regime: The results apply to type A Schubert varieties, their Bott-Samelson resolutions, and finite-dimensional representations of quivers over algebraically closed fields.
2502.11790.hypothesized_generalization: The construction suggests that resolutions of singularities for Schubert varieties in other Lie types, or more general Schubert varieties, can be realized as quiver Grassmannians of rigid representations of appropriate quivers with relations.

2502.11847.problem: The paper establishes an upper bound on the minimal log discrepancy of Fano cone singularities by relating it to the dimensions of moduli spaces of orbifold rational curves.
2502.11847.methods: The authors employ Mori's deformation theory of rational curves, symplectic field theory invariants, and the geometry of Deligne-Mumford stacks to analyze orbifold tangent bundles and twisted stable maps.
2502.11847.regime: The results apply to complex orbifolds with ample orbifold tangent bundles and isolated Fano cone singularities with cyclic quotient singularities.
2502.11847.hypothesized_generalization: The authors propose a characterization of weighted projective spaces using orbifold rational curves of minimal degree, suggesting that the equality case for their minimal log discrepancy bound occurs exclusively at smooth points.

2502.11950.problem: The paper aims to construct a motivic lift for the complex volume of hyperbolic three-manifolds and relate its Hodge realization to the geometry of the character variety.
2502.11950.methods: The authors construct a mixed Tate motive over the invariant trace field and analyze its limit mixed Hodge structure using the path torsor of the augmented character variety and the Beilinson regulator.
2502.11950.regime: The results apply to complete, finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifolds, particularly those with a single torus boundary under specific asymptotic conditions on the Chern-Simons invariant.
2502.11950.hypothesized_generalization: The construction suggests a broader parallel between the motivic theory of hyperbolic manifolds and the classical motivic theory of polylogarithms.

2502.12010.problem: The paper aims to prove the log-concavity of the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial for representable matroids and hyperplane arrangements.
2502.12010.methods: The authors relate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial to the multidegrees of the Gauss map of a pencil of hypersurfaces, utilizing logarithmic foliations and Hodge-Khovanskii-Teissier type inequalities.
2502.12010.regime: The results apply to central hyperplane arrangements and representable matroids over fields of characteristic zero.
2502.12010.hypothesized_generalization: The connection between characteristic polynomials and the multidegrees of rational maps suggests that other combinatorial invariants of matroids might be realized as geometric invariants of associated algebraic varieties.

2502.12075.problem: The paper investigates whether the Jordan-Hölder property holds for polarizable semiorthogonal decompositions of triangulated categories.
2502.12075.methods: The authors construct counterexamples by analyzing Bridgeland stability conditions and grading structures on Fukaya categories of surfaces with boundary, mapping them to representations of graded gentle algebras.
2502.12075.regime: The results apply to smooth and proper pre-triangulated dg-categories, specifically those arising as derived categories of coherent sheaves on smooth projective varieties.
2502.12075.hyposthesized_generalization: The findings suggest that the Jordan-Hölder property fails even under strong polarizability assumptions, hinting at a general obstruction to the existence of bounded t-structures on certain geometric triangulated categories.

2502.12136.problem: The construction of a functorial weight spectral sequence in p-adic cohomology for projective strictly semi-stable schemes over formal power series rings.
2502.12136.methods: Constructing the spectral sequence using the theory of arithmetic D-modules and proving the holonomicity of the unipotent nearby cycle functor up to shift.
2502.12136.regime: Projective strictly semi-stable schemes over a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with a perfect residue field of characteristic p.
2502.12136.thought_generalization: A fully developed formalism of log arithmetic D-modules that yields a complete six-functor formalism, duality, and pullback functoriality for p-adic weight spectral sequences.

2502.12162.problem: The paper establishes a systematic duality framework for non-smooth and non-proper algebraic structures, specifically characterizing how generalized Calabi-Yau, Gorenstein, and Frobenius conditions correspond under Koszul duality.
2502.12162.methods: The authors employ Koszul duality, bar and cobar constructions, and derived category theory to map properties between differential graded algebras and conilpotent differential graded coalgebras.
2502.12162.regime: The results apply to augmented differential graded algebras and conilpotent differential graded coalgebras over a fixed field, encompassing both smooth/proper and non-smooth/non-proper settings.
2502.12162.hypothesized_generalization: The correspondence hints at a broader derived deformation theory and a unified duality framework for singular geometric spaces and their noncommutative algebraic representations.

2502.12281.problem: The paper computes the orbifold Euler characteristic of the intersection of multiple double ramification loci in genus one.
2502.12281.methods: The authors employ a cut-and-paste recursion relation in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, combined with symmetric function theory and matrix minor analysis.
2502.12281.regime: The results apply to higher rank double ramification loci associated to integer matrices with zero-sum rows in genus one.
2502.12281.hypothesized_generalization: The authors outline an in-principle method to compute the orbifold Euler characteristic of double ramification loci in arbitrary genus using a stratification by Hurwitz spaces.

2502.12428.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of computationally identifying and constructing algebraic varieties (specifically K3 surfaces) that realize every theoretically possible height parameter over small finite fields.
2502.12428.methods: The authors accelerate a generalized Fedder's criterion by reformulating the bottleneck polynomial operations into parallelized matrix-vector multiplications and finite-field Fast Fourier Transforms implemented on GPU hardware.
2502.12428.regime: The computational results and algorithms are demonstrated for quartic K3 surfaces over the finite fields of order 5 and 7.
2502.12428.thought_or_generalization: The success of GPU-accelerated linear algebra and polynomial arithmetic in this context suggests that other computationally intensive problems in arithmetic geometry and commutative algebra over finite fields can be tractably solved using parallel GPU architectures.

2502.12815.problem: The paper aims to formalize and unify the mathematical foundations of positive geometries, which relate real semi-algebraic subsets of complex algebraic varieties to unique canonical meromorphic top-forms with prescribed logarithmic singularities.
2502.12815.methods: The framework integrates techniques from real, complex, and tropical algebraic geometry, combinatorics of polytopes and Schubert arrangements, and mixed Hodge theory to construct and analyze canonical differential forms and their associated period integrals.
2502.12815.regime: The mathematical structures apply to finite-dimensional complex projective varieties, Grassmannians, and convex polytopes, with physical realizations in tree-level scattering amplitudes, cosmological correlators, and statistical models.
2502.12815.hypothesized_generalization: The dual role of canonical forms as both physical amplitudes and universal barrier functions hints at a deeper, unified geometric framework linking quantum field theory, convex optimization, and Bayesian algebraic statistics.

2502.13050.problem: The paper addresses the problem of calculating the local intersection multiplicity (or Euler class localization) for isotropic sections of vector bundles equipped with a non-degenerate quadratic form.
2502.13050.methods: The authors develop orthogonal analogues of the classical Hopf index theorem, utilizing techniques such as cosection localization, projectivized normal cones, Clifford multiplication complexes, and equivariant torus actions.
2502.13050.regime: The results apply to isotropic sections of complex orthogonal vector bundles over a complex manifold, with specific topological refinements when the rank of the bundle is divisible by four.
2502.13050.hypod_generalization: The results suggest a generalized framework for computing virtual cycles and localized invariants in gauge theory and algebraic geometry where orthogonal or isotropic constraints are present.

2502.13087.problem: Constructing and characterizing a new class of algebraic surfaces of general type that are Lagrangian in their Albanese variety and have a canonical map of degree two onto a low-degree canonical surface with even nodes.
2502.13087.methods: Analyzing the Galois closure of a rational map on the product of two elliptic curves, utilizing the action of a Galois group on a Kummer four-fold, and applying Castelnuovo-de Franchis and semiregularity techniques.
2502.13087.regime: The construction applies to a very general abelian surface of type (1,3) and its associated hyperelliptic curves of geometric genus three.
2502.13087.hypothesized_generalization: The deformation of these surfaces to cases where their Albanese variety is no longer isogenous to a product, which may help prove the Hodge conjecture for a broader class of abelian four-folds.

2502.13099.problem: The paper establishes a unified framework to prove geometric and algebraic inequalities by mapping relations between intersection indices of divisors in algebraic geometry and mixed volumes of convex bodies in convex geometry.
2502.13099.methods: The authors utilize homogeneous polynomials on commutative semigroups, their polarizations, and the theory of Newton-Okounkov bodies to relate finite-dimensional spaces of rational functions to convex bodies.
2502.13099.regime: The results apply to finite-dimensional commutative semigroups, irreducible algebraic varieties over algebraically closed fields, and finite-dimensional convex bodies.
2502.13099.hypothesized_generalization: The equivalence suggests a deeper, axiomatic theory of mixed volumes and intersection indices that can be defined on arbitrary semigroups equipped with appropriate homogeneous functions.

2502.13121.problem: The paper aims to compute the volumes of specific strata of moduli spaces of quadratic differentials with odd singularities.
2502.13121.methods: The authors count square-tiled surfaces by analyzing integer metrics on ribbon graphs with odd valencies and determining their counting functions on the boundary walls where discontinuities occur.
2502.13121.regime: The results apply to odd strata of quadratic differentials with at least three singularities across arbitrary genus.
2502.13121.hypothesized_generalization: The volume formula and its constituent terms suggest a systematic way to compute large genus asymptotics for Masur–Veech volumes of odd strata.

2502.13305.problem: The paper investigates whether certain algebraic positivity and geometric intersection properties of homogeneous polynomials are preserved under variable-reduction operations like diagonalization.
2502.13305.methods: The authors analyze denormalized volume polynomials associated with projective varieties and divisor classes, using intersection theory, normalization, and differential operators to prove closure under diagonalization, products, and truncations.
2502.13305.regime: The results apply to homogeneous polynomials of arbitrary degree and dimension with non-negative coefficients, specifically in the context of algebraic geometry and combinatorial generating functions.
2502.13305.hypothesized_generalization: The preservation of volume polynomial properties under diagonalization hints that broader classes of Lorentzian and log-concave polynomials might share similar structural invariants under variable aggregation.

2502.13284.problem: The paper determines the uniruledness of certain moduli spaces of pointed spin curves.
2502.13284.methods: The proofs construct rational curves through generic points by utilizing dominant maps from projective bundles over moduli spaces of non-standard Nikulin surfaces.
2502.13284.regime: The results apply to moduli spaces of pointed spin curves of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points for specific small values of $g$ and $n$, specifically $(g,n) \in \{(2,1), (2,2), (3,1), (3,2), (4,1), (4,2), (5,1), (6,1), (7,1)\}$.
2502.13284.hypothesized_generalization: The dominance of maps from Nikulin-surface-derived bundles suggests a systematic way to establish the uniruledness or unirationality of moduli spaces of curves with theta characteristics for other low-genus cases.

2502.13315.problem: The paper establishes the foundational properties and compatibility of a specialized cohomology theory for non-Archimedean analytic spaces.
2502.13315.methods: The authors employ rigid analytic geometry, site-theoretic cohomology, and the geometry of log-schemes applied to sheaves on rigid spaces.
2502.13315.regime: The results apply to the setting of rigid analytic spaces over non-Archimedean local fields of mixed characteristic.
2502.13315.hypothesized_generalization: The foundational results lay the groundwork for a fully developed p-adic Hodge theory for general rigid analytic varieties.

2502.13356.problem: The paper aims to establish the splitting of the de Rham complex and the degeneration of the associated Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence for a broad class of algebraic varieties and stacks in positive characteristic.
2502.13356.methods: The authors utilize the stacky approach to de Rham cohomology, specifically exploiting the gerbe property of the de Rham stack and splitting the conjugate filtration on the Frobenius pullback of the complex.
2502.13356.regime: The results apply to smooth quasi-F-split varieties, smooth Artin stacks, and classifying stacks of reductive groups over perfect fields of positive characteristic.
2502.13356.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that many classical cohomological properties and decompositions of liftable varieties can be extended to more general stacky settings and weaker splitting structures using the geometry of the de Rham stack.

2502.13468.problem: The paper investigates the geometric and topological relationship between non-archimedean period domains and their associated combinatorial buildings beyond the classically understood fully decomposable cases.
2502.13468.methods: The authors construct continuous retraction maps and compare boundary structures using Berkovich analytic spaces, Bruhat-Tits buildings, and the geometry of flag varieties over non-archimedean local fields.
2502.13468.regime: The results apply to general connected reductive groups over finite extensions of p-adic fields, with explicit constructions detailed for general linear groups and specific cocharacters.
2502.13468.hyporhesized_generalization: The connection between period domains and buildings suggests a more general correspondence between the analytic geometry of p-adic symmetric spaces and the combinatorial geometry of Bruhat-Tits buildings for arbitrary reductive groups.

2502.13507.problem: The paper aims to generalize the concept of multiplicity and its associated upper bounds from fake weighted projective spaces to broader classes of algebraic varieties with well-behaved birational geometry.
2502.13507.methods: The authors introduce and analyze the weight group and weight modulus of complete toric varieties, utilizing combinatorial properties of fan matrices, Gale duality, and the Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky decomposition.
2502.13507.regime: The results apply to finite-dimensional Fano, Q-Gorenstein, and Q-Fano toric varieties, as well as Mori Dream Spaces, under various singularity conditions such as canonical singularities.
2502.13507.hypothesized_generalization: The bounds on multiplicity suggest a deeper, systematic relationship between the divisor class group structure, the anti-canonical volume, and the Picard number across general Mori Dream Spaces.

2502.13528.problem: The paper investigates how the properties of algebraic principal bundles (torsors) behave under the pullback of the Frobenius morphism in positive characteristic.
2502.13528.methods: The authors apply Frobenius descent techniques to analyze the preservation and triviality of principal G-bundles over algebraic varieties.
2502.13528.regime: The results apply to the setting of algebraic geometry over fields of prime characteristic p > 0.
2502.13528.hypothesized_generalization: The behavior of these torsors under Frobenius descent hints at a more general correspondence between vector bundles with flat connections and representations of the fundamental group scheme in positive characteristic.

2502.13545.problem: The paper establishes a mirror symmetry correspondence for specific blowups of Grassmannian manifolds, identifying the appropriate Landau-Ginzburg models that serve as their mirror duals.
2502.13545.methods: The authors construct superpotential functions on algebraic tori and analyze their critical points using toric geometry and the combinatorics of Newton-Okounkov bodies.
2502.13545.regime: The results apply to Fano varieties obtained by blowing up Grassmannians along specific subvarieties, operating within the framework of complex algebraic geometry.
2502.13545.hypothesized_generalization: The construction suggests a systematic way to define mirror duals for a wider class of non-toric Fano manifolds obtained via birational modifications of homogeneous spaces.

2502.13558.problem: The paper investigates the validity of Galkin's lower bound conjecture, the Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani conjecture, and a newly proposed blow-up inequality for the quantum cohomology of specific Fano manifolds.
2502.13558.methods: The authors compute the quantum multiplication by the first Chern class using genus-zero, two-point Gromov-Witten invariants, blow-up formulas, and Perron's theorem on positive matrices.
2502.13558.regime: The results apply to four-dimensional smooth quadrics blown up at a point or along a projective plane.
2502.13558.hypothesized_generalization: The results support a general conjecture that the spectral radius of the quantum multiplication operator of a Fano manifold is strictly greater than that of its Fano blow-up along a smooth subvariety of codimension at least two.

2502.13582.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of computing and analyzing high-dimensional physical observables, such as scattering amplitudes and cosmological correlators, by reformulating them through geometric and algebraic structures rather than summing over traditional perturbative expansions.
2502.13582.methods: The approach utilizes positive geometries, canonical differential forms, and Feynman integrals to map physical interaction probabilities to the volumes and residues of semi-algebraic varieties.
2502.13582.regime: The framework applies to both subatomic particle interactions in Minkowski space and large-scale cosmological structures originating from early-universe quantum field theories.
2502.13582.hypotheses_generalization: The dual application of positive geometry to both particle physics and cosmology hints at a unified, spacetime-independent mathematical framework for describing quantum field theories across all physical scales.

2502.13800.problem: Determining the conditions under which a rational group action on the generic fiber of a family of varieties extends to a regular action on a minimal model of the family.
2502.13800.methods: Applying minimal model theory and singularity analysis to terminal and log canonical pairs over a base scheme to establish the regularity of rational actions and the existence of equivariant completions.
2502.13800.regime: Projective minimal models and smooth group schemes with connected fibers, primarily over fields of characteristic zero or under conditions where minimal models are known to exist.
2502.13800.hyporhesized_generalization: The existence of equivariant completions for rational actions of non-affine group schemes on normal projective varieties in arbitrary characteristic.

2502.13815.problem: The paper aims to classify and characterize the algebraic structure, Weierstrass semigroups, and automorphism groups of maximal function fields of the third largest possible genus over finite fields of characteristic three.
2502.13815.methods: The authors analyze divisors of functions, differentials, and local power series expansions to compute Weierstrass semigroups and determine the full automorphism group of the function field.
2502.13815.regime: The results apply to algebraic function fields over finite fields of square cardinality $q^2$ where $q$ is a power of 3.
2502.13815.hypothesized_generalization: The detailed characterization of Weierstrass semigroups and automorphism groups may provide the necessary invariants to prove the uniqueness, up to isomorphism, of maximal function fields achieving the third largest possible genus.

2502.13882.problem: The lack of a unified geometric framework to define loop spaces for elliptic curves that generalizes the rational and trigonometric loop spaces associated with additive and multiplicative group schemes.
2502.13882.methods: The authors construct a functor from algebraic stacks to derived stacks with an action of an elliptic curve, utilizing 1-categorical Cartier duality and convolution tensor categories of coherent sheaves with 1-dimensional support.
2502.13882.regime: The construction applies to derived algebraic geometry and stack theory over a field of characteristic zero, specifically focusing on global quotient stacks and schemes of finite type.

2502.13892.problem: The difficulty of defining enumerative invariants and stability structures for general algebraic stacks where points have non-trivial, positive-dimensional automorphism groups.
2502.13892.methods: Analyzing the combinatorial structures of the component lattice of stacks of graded and filtered points, and proving constancy, finiteness, and associativity theorems for these structures.
2502.13892.regime: Algebraic stacks over a field, generalizing from linear moduli stacks of abelian categories to general quotient and shifted symplectic stacks.
2502.13892.hypothesized_generalization: A unified framework for constructing intrinsic enumerative theories and stability data across arbitrary algebraic stacks, extending beyond Calabi-Yau abelian categories.

2502.13937.problem: The paper aims to compute explicit combinatorial formulas for generating functions that count quasimaps to a class of geometric spaces whose torus fixed points are not necessarily zero-dimensional.
2502.13937.methods: The authors employ localization formulas, minuscule posets, and skew-Macdonald polynomials to evaluate the generating functions as products of q-binomial series.
2502.13937.regime: The results apply to type D Nakajima quiver varieties with framing vectors restricted to minuscule vertices, including the special case of zero-dimensional varieties.
2502.13937.hypothesized_generalization: The factorization of these vertex functions hints at a deeper connection to integrable probabilistic models, specifically half-space Macdonald processes.

2502.13903.problem: The paper establishes algebraic criteria to determine when a set of locally nilpotent derivations on an integral domain forms a compatible tuple, which is a key condition for proving the algebraic density property.
2502.13903.methods: The authors analyze the compatibility of derivations by studying the structure of the subalgebra they generate and the properties of their associated grading on normal affine domains over fields of characteristic zero.
2502.13903.regime: The results apply to normal affine integral domains over any field of characteristic zero, with a particular focus on those admitting nontrivial fundamental pairs of derivations.
2502.13903.hypothesized_generalization: The algebraic criteria developed for compatible tuples of derivations could potentially be generalized to characterize the algebraic density property for broader classes of non-reductive affine homogeneous spaces and varieties with higher-dimensional group actions.

2502.14109.problem: The paper aims to extend a classical boundary-extension construction for geometric spaces to a non-Archimedean setting, specifically establishing a continuous extension of period mappings to a boundary for local geometric structures.
2502.14109.methods: The authors employ p-adic geometry and the theory of local Shimura varieties, analyzing the asymptotic behavior of period maps near the boundary of the domain.
2502.14109.regime: The results apply to local Shimura varieties over p-adic local fields, operating within the framework of non-Archimedean analytic geometry.
2502.14109.hypothesized_generalization: The construction hints at a general theory of compactifications and boundary behavior for wider classes of p-adic period domains and moduli spaces of local shtukas.

2502.14408.problem: The paper analyzes the local intersection-theoretical and geometric properties of approximate roots of polynomials defining plane curves with a single branch at infinity.
2502.14408.methods: The authors introduce the concept of semiroots to study these approximate roots using Newton-Puiseux parameterizations, intersection numbers, and minimal resolutions of singularities.
2502.14408.regime: The results apply to bivariate complex polynomials defining algebraic curves with one place at infinity, specifically focusing on their local properties in the complex affine plane.
2502.14408.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint at generalizations to quasi-ordinary singularities of higher-dimensional hypersurfaces and to curves defined over fields of positive characteristic.

2502.14530.problem: Establishing the projectivity of moduli spaces of stable objects when the underlying moduli problem lacks a global geometric invariant theory (GIT) formulation.
2502.14530.methods: Constructing and analyzing the positivity of explicit determinantal line bundles on algebraic stacks using restriction theorems and relative Quot scheme stratifications.
2502.14530.regime: Smooth projective threefolds over the complex numbers, specifically under the assumption of coprime rank and degree where strictly semistable objects do not exist.
2502.14530.hyporhesized_generalization: The existence of projective coarse moduli spaces for stable objects in more general polynomial or Bridgeland stability conditions on higher-dimensional varieties without GIT.

2502.14414.problem: Constructing and evaluating the minimum distance of linear evaluation codes generated by evaluating low-dimensional subspaces of symmetric polynomials over finite fields.
2502.14414.methods: Mapping symmetric polynomials to standard multivariate polynomials via elementary symmetric polynomials, combined with analyzing the intersection of algebraic varieties over finite fields.
2502.14414.regime: Finite fields of odd order, specifically focusing on low-dimensional linear systems of symmetric polynomials in three variables.
2502.14414.hypothesized_generalization: The weight distributions and minimum distances of these codes are conjectured to be determined by the intersection geometry of higher-dimensional algebraic varieties over finite fields, potentially yielding locally recoverable codes.

2502.14858.problem: The paper computes the continuous Galois cohomology of valuation fields with coefficients in their completed algebraic closures, extending classical results from the discrete to the non-discrete valuation setting.
2502.14858.methods: The authors utilize ramified base change theorems, cotangent complexes, and integral Breuil-Kisin-Fargues twists to analyze the cohomology of Henselian valuation fields of arbitrary height.
2502.14858.regime: The results apply to Henselian valuation fields of height $h$ over a $p$-adic local field, covering both arithmetic (discrete-like) and geometric (pre-perfectoid-like) settings, including finitely generated extensions of transcendental degree $d$.
2502.14858.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques suggest a path toward developing a general non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and constructing Hodge-Tate spectral sequences for non-smooth proper $p$-adic varieties.

2502.14646.problem: The paper determines the eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and characteristic polynomials of the linear operators defined by quantum multiplication on the quantum cohomology of odd-dimensional quadrics, and verifies a lower bound conjecture on the largest real eigenvalue of the first Chern class.
2502.14646.methods: The authors analyze the spectral properties of quantum multiplication matrices by performing row reduction on structured matrices, computing determinants, and verifying simultaneous diagonalizability of the operators.
2502.14646.regime: The results apply to the small quantum cohomology ring of odd-dimensional complex quadrics of arbitrary dimension.
2502.14646.hypothesized_generalization: The validation of the eigenvalue lower bound supports the general conjecture that the largest real eigenvalue of the first Chern class of any Fano variety is bounded below by its dimension plus one, scaled by the index.

2502.15052.problem: The paper aims to explicitly match the transcendental cohomology of K3 surfaces having complex multiplication of large degree with algebraic Hecke quasi-characters.
2502.15052.methods: The authors employ a combination of algorithmic computations in Magma, period lattice approximations, and the analysis of Galois representations on transcendental lattices and Jacobians of genus 3 curves.
2502.15052.regime: The results apply to specific families of K3 surfaces defined over the rational numbers with complex multiplication by cyclic sextic fields of large degree.
2502.15052.hypothesized_generalization: The findings provide substantial evidence that a power of the transcendental Galois representation of these K3 surfaces corresponds to the Jacobian of a genus 3 curve under the Kuga-Satake correspondence.

2502.15101.problem: The paper investigates the structure and transitivity properties of the holomorphic automorphism group of a class of complex affine surfaces with isolated singularities and a natural volume form.
2502.15101.methods: The authors construct complete holomorphic vector fields from algebraic Hamiltonian functions to establish the Hamiltonian and symplectic density properties on singular algebraic varieties.
2502.15101.regime: The results apply to complex two-dimensional affine surfaces defined by a Markov-type quadratic-cubic equation, specifically focusing on their regular loci and discrete subsets.
2502.15101.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that the dichotomy between discrete algebraic automorphism groups and infinite-dimensional holomorphic automorphism groups, along with the existence of tame discrete orbits, generalizes to wider classes of affine surfaces with circular boundary divisors.

2502.15126.problem: The paper aims to compute the structure constants for the intersection of Schubert classes in the cohomology of two-step flag varieties.
2502.15126.methods: The authors utilize representation theory of quivers and the geometry of their representation spaces to establish bijective correspondences between intersection points and specific algebraic structures.
2502.15126.regime: The results apply to partial flag varieties with two steps, corresponding to representations of A3-type quivers.
2502.15126.hypothesized_generalization: The geometric and quiver-theoretic methods developed here could generalize to provide combinatorial rules for multi-step flag varieties and more general quiver representation spaces.

2502.15175.problem: The paper investigates the algebraic and geometric structure of the coordinate rings corresponding to the open complements of canonical closed subschemes within noncommutative projective lines.
2502.15175.methods: The authors analyze the localization of noncommutative symmetric algebras of two-sided vector spaces of rank 2 by inverting normal families of elements to study the resulting indexed algebras.
2502.15175.regime: The results apply to simple, two-sided vector spaces of dimension 2 over a pair of fields, corresponding to both algebraic and non-algebraic bimodules.
2502.15175.hyporhesized_generalization: The dichotomy between algebraic and non-algebraic bimodules suggests a broader classification of noncommutative curves and their coordinate rings based on the dynamical behavior of associated Galois involutions.

2502.15513.problem: Determine the maximum possible minimal dimension of a faithful matrix representation for any algebraic torus of a given dimension across all possible base fields.
2502.15513.methods: Analyzing the symmetric rank and integral representation theory of finite matrix groups acting on free abelian groups of finite rank.
2502.15513.regime: Arbitrary base fields, with specific exact results established for number fields and low-dimensional or prime-dimensional tori.
2502.15513.hypothesized_generalization: The established lower bounds on the maximal representation dimension are conjectured to be exact for all positive integer dimensions.

2502.15195.problem: The paper characterizes the topological structure and local deformations of bounded planar regions bounded by intersecting circles under sequential additions of new circles.
2502.15195.methods: The authors analyze the quotient spaces of the regions under coordinate projections, representing them as labeled Poincaré-Reeb graphs, and track their combinatorial changes using singularity theory of differentiable maps.
2502.15195.dev_regime: The results apply to finite, normally inductive arrangements of circles in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane and their associated cell complexes.
2502.15195.hypothesized_generalization: The local graph-deformation rules suggest a systematic way to reconstruct the topology of higher-dimensional manifolds and their real algebraic projections from lower-dimensional combinatorial data.

2502.15517.problem: The paper aims to determine the algebraic structure and generators of the cohomological Hall algebras associated to the category of zero-dimensional sheaves supported on a weighted projective curve.
2502.15517.methods: The authors construct these algebras using the geometry of moduli spaces of torsion sheaves and analyze their generators by mapping them to loop algebras of Kac-Moody Lie algebras.
2502.15517.regime: The results apply to the category of coherent torsion sheaves on smooth, one-dimensional orbifold curves over the complex numbers.
2502.15517.hypothesized_generalization: The algebraic isomorphism suggests a broader correspondence between the cohomological Hall algebras of curves and the quantum toroidal algebras associated to higher-dimensional geometric structures.

2502.15550.problem: The paper aims to determine the precise multiplicity of a specific Schubert class in the quantum product of a divisor class and a point class within the quantum cohomology ring of a non-homogeneous variety.
2502.15550.methods: The authors compute curve neighborhoods of Schubert varieties by analyzing the combinatorics of chains and edge degrees in the moment graph of the partial flag variety.
2502.15550.regime: The results apply to the odd symplectic partial flag variety parameterizing isotropic subspace sequences of dimension step two, indexed by signed permutations.
2502.15550.hypothesized_generalization: The existence of multiple irreducible components in the curve neighborhoods suggests a general framework for predicting the exact coefficients in quantum Chevalley formulas for wider classes of non-homogeneous flag varieties.

2502.15621.problem: Reconstructing a geometric space from its underlying triangulated category under relaxed projectivity and ampleness conditions.
2502.15621.methods: Extending the Matsui spectrum construction to polarized triangulated categories equipped with a designated autoequivalence that generalizes the Serre functor.
2502.15621.regime: Gorenstein projective and proper varieties over algebraically closed fields, as well as noncommutative projective schemes.
2502.15621.hypothesized_generalization: A unified framework for homological mirror symmetry and birational geometry where geometric properties of mirror partners are encoded as topological properties of polarized triangulated categories.

2502.15674.problem: The paper determines the minimal size of a parametric set of extensions over a rational function field required to specialize to all Galois extensions of a given base field for a specified finite group.
2502.15674.methods: The authors analyze R-equivalence classes of torsors under finite group schemes, utilizing Galois cohomology, relative Brauer groups, and the decomposition of semidirect products with cyclic kernels.
2502.15674.regime: The results apply to finite Galois extensions of fields, with a particular focus on number fields, p-adic fields, and rational function fields.
2502.15674.thought: The authors hypothesize that the finiteness of R-equivalence classes is preserved under split extensions with abelian kernels for all finite solvable groups over number fields.

2502.15977.problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous geometric and combinatorial framework for classifying and analyzing superschemes that possess a reduced structure, specifically in the context of toric supervarieties.
2502.15977.methods: The author utilizes combinatorial techniques, such as super-fans and super-polytopes, to study the algebraic and geometric properties of toric superschemes.
2502.15977.regime: The results apply to the setting of algebraic supergeometry, specifically focusing on finite-dimensional toric superschemes and their underlying reduced classical schemes.
2502.15977.hypothesized_generalization: The combinatorial classification of toric supervarieties hints at a broader dictionary between tropical supergeometry and the classification of more general spherical supervarieties.

2502.16009.problem: The paper investigates the asymptotic transitivity of automorphism group actions on the finite field points of character varieties as the field order approaches infinity.
2502.16009.methods: The authors employ arithmetic stratification of character varieties based on matrix stabilizer types under conjugation, combined with counting techniques for characteristic polynomials over finite fields.
