2502.16009.regime: The results apply to the action of the outer automorphism group of a free group of rank two on the SL(2, q)-character variety as the finite field order q approaches infinity.
2502.16009.hypothesized_generalization: The authors suggest that these arithmetic dynamics can be generalized to character varieties of free groups of higher rank and can provide insight into the topological properties of character varieties over fields of characteristic zero.

2502.16026.problem: The paper aims to find tighter, more computable upper bounds for the Bieri-Neumann-Strebel-Renz (BNSR) invariants of a space, which characterize its geometric finiteness properties.
2502.16026.methods: The authors analyze the tropicalization of homology jump ideals with integral coefficients, leveraging valuation theory and the algebraic properties of modules over finitely generated abelian groups.
2502.16026.regime: The results apply to connected finite CW complexes with finitely generated abelianizations, specifically focusing on the structure of their homology jump loci and associated tropical varieties.
2502.16026.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that the geometric finiteness of a group can be completely characterized by the intersection of tropical varieties of its homology jump loci across all prime and zero characteristics.

2502.16322.problem: The paper aims to classify and describe the irreducible components and local structure of the boundary divisors in the compactified moduli space of a specific class of algebraic surfaces.
2502.16322.methods: The authors analyze the minimal desingularizations of stable surfaces, construct explicit one-parameter flat deformations, and compute the tangent and obstruction spaces of Gorenstein deformations.
2502.16322.regime: The results apply asymptotically to stable Horikawa surfaces of the second kind with $K^2 = 2p_g - 3$ for sufficiently large values of the geometric genus $p_g$.
2502.16322.hypothesized_generalization: The classification of boundary divisors via index 2 T-singularities suggests a general framework for describing the codimension-one boundary of the KSBA moduli space for other classes of surfaces of general type.

2502.16441.problem: The paper aims to enumerate and describe the irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties and compare their structure to that of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties.
2502.16441.methods: The authors utilize reduction paths within reduction trees to encode Deligne-Lusztig reduction steps and analyze the action of centralizers on the irreducible components of affine Springer fibers.
2502.16441.regime: The results apply to arbitrary reductive groups in both equal and mixed characteristic settings, specifically focusing on regular semisimple elements with integral Newton vectors.
2502.16441.hypothesized_generalization: The alignment of orbit counts for sufficiently large parameters hints at a deeper, unified geometric or representation-theoretic connection between affine Lusztig and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties.

2502.16543.problem: The paper establishes the existence and properties of polynomial structures that count the filtrations of objects with specified sub-quotient structures within a class of hereditary categories.
2502.16543.methods: The authors employ Hall algebra techniques, homological algebra, and the representation theory of weighted projective lines to analyze the decomposition of extensions of coherent sheaves.
2502.16543.regime: The results apply to the category of coherent sheaves over a weighted projective line defined over a finite field.
2502.16543.hypothesized_generalization: The existence of these polynomials hints at a unified deformation theory or quantum group-like structure underlying more general classes of non-commutative curves and higher-dimensional hereditary categories.

2502.16571.problem: The paper addresses the lack of stability under arbitrary pullbacks for certain sheaves of meromorphic forms on singular spaces that extend holomorphically to any desingularization.
2502.16571.methods: The author constructs a pullback morphism and higher direct images by integrating meromorphic forms over fibers along exceptional divisors of desingularizations and applying relative duality theory.
2502.16571.regime: The results apply to arbitrary morphisms between reduced complex analytic spaces of pure dimension.
2502.16571.hypothesized_generalization: The construction suggests that integration over exceptional fibers can be generalized to define functorial pullbacks for other classes of singular differential forms on arbitrary complex spaces.

2502.16582.problem: Determining the conditions under which a piecewise-linear tropical subvariety can be lifted to an analytic subvariety in a corresponding complex or rigid analytic space.
2502.16582.methods: Comparing algebraic deformation theory of sheaf pushforwards and logarithmic geometry on the algebraic side with the symplectic deformation theory of Fukaya algebras and bounding cochains on the Lagrangian side.
2502.16582.regime: Three-valent smooth tropical curves embedded in three-dimensional integral metric affine manifolds.
2502.16582.hypothesized_generalization: A systematic dictionary via homological mirror symmetry that equates the vanishing of algebraic deformation obstructions for tropical curves with the unobstructedness of corresponding Lagrangian submanifolds in dual torus fibrations.

2502.16727.problem: The paper addresses the problem of computing universal cohomological obstructions that determine when and where specific local degeneracies of mappings between spaces must occur globally.
2502.16727.methods: The approach utilizes equivariant cohomology, localization techniques, and Hilbert schemes of points to compute characteristic classes and Thom polynomials for map-germs.
2502.16727.regime: The results apply to the global topology of real and complex mappings between manifolds, primarily within the complex analytic and algebraic geometry categories.
2502.16727.hypothesized_generalization: The synthesis of localization and Hilbert schemes hints at a unified framework for solving broader enumeration problems across contemporary Schubert calculus, moduli stacks, and quantum integrable systems.

2502.16742.problem: The paper aims to characterize the geometric and lattice structures of curve neighborhoods for subvarieties in a non-homogeneous setting, and to verify a spectral property of quantum multiplication by the first Chern class.
2502.16742.methods: The authors analyze the irreducible components of curve neighborhoods using lattice theory and prove a spectral conjecture by reducing it to a graph-theoretic check on the cycle lengths of the quantum Bruhat graph.
2502.16742.regime: The results apply to the family of odd symplectic partial flag manifolds, which represent a class of non-homogeneous, Fano, complex varieties.
2502.16742.hypothesized_generalization: The success of the graph-theoretic criterion suggests that the connection between the Perron-Frobenius properties of quantum cohomology and the connectivity of the quantum Bruhat graph extends to more general classes of non-homogeneous Fano varieties.

2502.16956.problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which the automorphism and birational automorphism groups of various classes of geometric spaces possess the Jordan property, which bounds the size of their finite subgroups.
2502.16956.methods: The authors analyze group extensions, canonical geometric fibrations, and the structure of connected components of automorphism groups using Hilbert schemes and Douady spaces.
2502.16956.regime: The results apply to algebraic varieties, projective varieties, and compact complex manifolds, primarily in characteristic zero but with extensions to positive characteristics.
2502.16956.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that the Jordan property can be generalized to broader classes of non-projective compact complex manifolds and general smooth manifolds under continuous group actions.

2502.16974.problem: The paper aims to formulate and analyze a stronger, logarithmic analogue of the Tate conjecture on algebraic cycles over finite fields, and to relate it to the weight-monodromy conjecture.
2502.16974.methods: The authors construct a log Tate curve over a finite field as a log scheme, utilize the isogeny of these curves, and analyze the Galois and monodromy actions on their log étale cohomology and homotopy K-theory.
2502.16974.regime: The results apply to projective vertical log smooth fs log schemes over a standard log point with a finite residue field.
2502.16974.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest the existence of a unique 'monodromy cycle' in the K-groups of log modifications that induces the monodromy operator on log étale cohomology, hinting at a deeper formulation of log motives.

2502.17031.problem: The paper investigates whether structural properties of algebraic hypersurfaces, specifically the freeness of their associated Milnor algebras, are preserved under dimension-raising product constructions.
2502.17031.methods: The authors construct product hypersurfaces from reduced plane curves and analyze the minimal graded free resolutions of their Milnor algebras using algebraic syzygies.
2502.17031.regime: The results apply to reduced plane curves and hyperplane arrangements over the complex numbers, specifically scaling from three-dimensional to higher-dimensional projective spaces.
2502.17031.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest that counterexamples to structural freeness conjectures in lower dimensions inductively propagate to all higher dimensions.

2502.17102.problem: The paper addresses the problem of systematically computing and tracking topological and algebraic invariants of singular curves under sequence-based resolution processes.
2502.17102.methods: The authors utilize combinatorial tree structures and valuation-theoretic models to encode the step-by-step evolution of geometric invariants across successive blow-ups.
2502.17102.regime: The results apply to local singularities of algebraic curves over fields of arbitrary characteristic, including positive characteristic.
2502.17102.hypothesized_generalization: The framework suggests that complex resolution processes in higher dimensions can be decomposed into discrete, algorithmic networks of simpler combinatorial operations.

2502.17148.problem: Determining whether differential forms defined on the smooth locus of a singular variety can be extended to logarithmic forms on a resolution of singularities.
2502.17148.methods: Applying algebraic techniques in positive characteristic, specifically strong F-regularity, quasi-F-injectivity, and the Cartier operator, to analyze the surjectivity of restriction maps on differential sheaves.
2502.17148.regime: Algebraic varieties over perfect fields of positive characteristic, specifically focusing on strongly F-regular singularities in arbitrary dimensions and klt threefolds in characteristic greater than five.
2502.17148.hyporhesized_generalization: The results suggest that strong F-regularity serves as the correct positive-characteristic analogue to klt singularities for extension theorems of differential forms, and that free tangent sheaves in this setting imply local Frobenius liftability rather than smoothness.

2502.17194.problem: The paper investigates the algebraic independence of multiple distinct solutions to a system of non-linear ordinary differential equations.
2502.17194.methods: The authors combine model-theoretic techniques of strong minimality and geometric triviality with Puiseux series expansions to analyze the differential fields generated by the solutions.
2502.17194.regime: The results apply to the classical two-dimensional Lotka-Volterra system of autonomous differential equations over a differential field of characteristic zero, under non-degeneracy conditions on the system's parameters.
2502.17194.hypothesized_generalization: The combination of model-theoretic strong minimality and valuation theory could be generalized to prove the algebraic independence of solutions for higher-dimensional autonomous polynomial differential systems.

2502.17236.problem: The paper establishes a precise equivalence between higher-genus descendant logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants of log Calabi-Yau surfaces and combinatorial invariants defined via quantum scattering diagrams.
2502.17236.methods: The authors use degeneration formulas in logarithmic Gromov-Witten theory, factorization of quantum scattering diagrams, and refined descendant tropical correspondence theorems to relate algebraic invariants to tropical curve counts.
2502.17236.regime: The results apply to higher-genus curves with descendant insertions on log Calabi-Yau surfaces, specifically Looijenga pairs, in the context of the Gross-Siebert program.
2502.17236.hypothesized_generalization: The authors suggest generalizing the correspondence to honest threefolds and using type III degenerations of K3 surfaces to probe their enumerative geometry with descendants.

2502.17404.problem: The paper aims to show that the abstractly defined p-adic André periods of mixed Tate motives over a residue field coincide with the classical p-adic periods constructed via p-adic iterated integrals and Coleman-Besser functions.
2502.17404.methods: The author compares different fiber functors and Tannakian Galois groups associated with categories of mixed Tate motives over number fields and their residue fields, utilizing the Berthelot comparison isomorphism to relate crystalline and de Rham realizations.
2502.17404.regime: The results apply to mixed Tate motives over number fields, their localizations, and their residue fields of characteristic p.
2502.17404.hypothesized_generalization: The comparison of André periods and classical p-adic periods hints at a general compatibility between Tannakian formal period rings and p-adic Hodge theory comparison isomorphisms for larger categories of mixed motives.

2502.17996.problem: The paper addresses the problem of simplifying a morphism from a three-dimensional space to a two-dimensional space into a monomial form through a sequence of blow-ups.
2502.17996.methods: The approach utilizes local valuation theory and resolution of singularities applied to algebraic varieties and their morphisms.
2502.17996.regime: The result applies to algebraic varieties over fields of characteristic zero, specifically mapping from dimension three to dimension two.
2502.17996.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques suggest a potential generalization to monomialization of morphisms between algebraic varieties of arbitrary dimensions.

2502.18084.problem: The paper aims to determine the exact number of codewords of minimum and next-to-minimum Hamming weights for a class of evaluation codes defined over hypersimplices, as well as to characterize the polynomials that generate these extremal weight codewords.
2502.18084.methods: The authors employ algebraic and geometric techniques, specifically analyzing the action of variable permutations and monomial isomorphisms on homogeneous monomially square-free polynomials evaluated over an affine torus.
2502.18084.regime: The results apply to toric codes associated with $d$-hypersimplices in $n$-dimensional space, specifically under the parameter constraints where the degree $d$ satisfies $2 \le d \le n-2$.
2502.18084.hyped_generalization: The characterization of extremal codewords suggests a broader geometric correspondence where hypersurfaces of a given degree that maximize intersections with an algebraic torus must structurally decompose into specific hyperplane arrangements.

2502.18088.problem: The paper addresses the problem of proving the existence of hypersurfaces of a given degree that vanish on a fixed set of points and possess a high-multiplicity singularity at a general point.
2502.18088.methods: The authors construct and analyze the determinant of a square interpolation matrix whose entries are bihomogeneous polynomials in the coordinates of the fixed points and the general point.
2502.18088.regime: The results apply to finite configurations of points in low-dimensional projective spaces, specifically projective planes and three-dimensional projective spaces over any field.
2502.18088.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hypothesize a deeper connection between the weak combinatorics of point arrangements and the splitting types of their associated logarithmic or syzygy vector bundles.

2502.18203.problem: The paper characterizes the mapping between a moduli space of complex geometric structures and their metric limits under collapsing, specifically determining the surjectivity and fiber sizes of this boundary map.
2502.18203.methods: The authors analyze the monodromy representations, twist transformations, and affine flat coordinates of special Kähler structures on Riemann surfaces.
2502.18203.regime: The results apply to the collapsing limits of hyperkähler metrics on Jacobian elliptic K3 surfaces converging to singular special Kähler structures.
2502.18203.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest a natural stratification of the moduli space of Jacobian elliptic K3 surfaces based on the uniqueness of the underlying integral structures of their metric limits.

2502.18250.problem: The paper addresses the problem of finding an algebraic solution to a topological problem, specifically the existence of certain mathematical structures, by translating it into an algebraic language.
2502.18250.methods: The paper uses K-theory, Jouanolou devices (affine vector bundle torsors), and motivic vector bundles to establish existence results and isomorphisms between different categories of sheaves.
2502.18250.regime: The results apply to regular noetherian schemes, quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with ample families of invertible sheaves, and projective varieties over a field.
2502.18250.hypothesized_generalization: The paper hints that any motivic vector bundle on a scheme might be algebraic, and that a key theorem regarding descent data for locally free sheaves might extend to any dimension.

2502.18276.problem: The paper addresses the problem of understanding and counting solutions for systems of polynomial equations, particularly when there are 'excess' intersections, which implies a deviation from expected behavior in the number of solutions.
2502.18276.methods: The paper employs techniques from algebraic geometry, likely involving concepts such as intersection theory and enumerative geometry, to analyze the properties of polynomial systems and their solution sets.
2502.18276.regime: The results apply to systems of polynomials, which are fundamental objects in algebraic geometry, and are relevant in contexts where precise counting of solutions and understanding intersection behavior is critical.
2502.18276.hypothesized_generalization: The paper's findings on breaking symmetry in excess intersection suggest a broader principle for analyzing and predicting the behavior of solutions in complex algebraic systems, potentially leading to more robust methods for counting and characterizing solutions in various mathematical and computational domains.

2502.18441.problem: The paper establishes a precise connection between the intersection numbers of multiple line bundles on an algebraic variety and the mixed volumes of their corresponding convex bodies.
2502.18441.methods: The authors construct specific admissible flags using Bertini's theorem and apply induction on the variety's dimension alongside a slice formula for Newton-Okounkov bodies.
2502.18441.regime: The results apply to ample and big line bundles on irreducible projective varieties of arbitrary dimension, with extensions to normal varieties.
2502.18441.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that general inequalities for mixed volumes of convex bodies can be systematically translated into geometric inequalities for intersection numbers of nef line bundles.

2502.18360.problem: The paper aims to determine which vector bundles obtained via Schur functors from a restricted tautological quotient bundle on a specific class of high-dimensional algebraic varieties are modular and polystable, and to compute their cohomology.
2502.18360.methods: The authors analyze the restriction of the tautological quotient bundle from a Grassmannian to a Debarre-Voisin fourfold, applying Schur functors and resolving the resulting sheaves using Koszul complexes.
2502.18360.regime: The results apply to very general Debarre-Voisin hyperkähler fourfolds of K3^[2]-type embedded in a Grassmannian of 3-planes in a 10-dimensional vector space.
2502.18360.hypotheses_generalization: The identical cohomological values obtained suggest a deformation equivalence between corresponding Schur functors of restricted quotient bundles across different models of K3^[2]-type hyperkähler manifolds.

2502.18751.problem: The paper characterizes and classifies low-dimensional complex spaces whose higher homotopy groups have a finite total rank.
2502.18751.methods: The authors analyze topological properties of Stein surfaces and affine varieties using algebraic and analytic fibrations, ramified coverings, and Nori's lemma.
2502.18751.regime: The results apply to complex Stein spaces of arbitrary dimension, with a particular focus on smooth complex affine surfaces of non-general type.
2502.18751.hypothesized_generalization: The dichotomy between finite homotopy rank-sum and exponential growth of homotopy groups may extend to broader classes of non-compact complex manifolds or singular analytic spaces.

2502.18784.problem: The paper aims to establish general topological criteria for when a spectrum constructed from a category is sober or spectral, and to determine when there exists a topological immersion from a subcategory's spectrum into the ambient category's spectrum.
2502.18784.methods: The authors generalize Matsui and Takahashi's support theory to extriangulated categories, utilizing Hochster dual topologies and universal reconstruction maps to analyze closed and open supports.
2502.18784.regime: The results apply to extriangulated categories, which unify and generalize the structures of both abelian and triangulated categories, particularly in the presence of finite group actions.
2502.18784.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint that many geometric reconstruction theorems in algebraic geometry and representation theory can be unified under a single topological framework of support data on extriangulated categories.

2502.18800.problem: Extending the existence of good minimal models to compact Kähler klt pairs under a projective map to their Albanese variety, where the standard cone theorem is unavailable.
2502.18800.methods: Running a relative minimal model program over the Albanese variety, establishing a substitute for the cone theorem, and adapting generic vanishing and Iitaka fibration techniques to the analytic setting.
2502.18800.regime: Compact Kähler varieties with projective Albanese maps, operating in the setting of higher-dimensional complex analytic geometry.
2502.18800.hypothesized_generalization: The results suggest that the minimal model program and the existence of good minimal models can be fully established for arbitrary compact Kähler varieties without requiring projectivity assumptions.

2502.18813.problem: Determine the conditions under which a higher-dimensional algebraic variety can be decomposed as the coordinate-wise product of lower-dimensional varieties.
2502.18813.methods: Analyzing the smoothness, tangency, and intersection properties of projective varieties under coordinate-wise rational maps, combined with matrix algebra on the defining quadratic forms.
2502.18813.regime: Low-dimensional algebraic varieties, specifically quadratic and higher-degree surfaces, embedded in three-dimensional projective space.
2502.18813.hypothesized_generalization: The non-transversal intersection of a surface with coordinate hyperplanes generalizes to higher-degree surfaces and higher-dimensional varieties decomposed as coordinate-wise products of lines and curves.

2502.18894.problem: The paper characterizes the space of stability conditions and the behavior of stable objects on a specific class of algebraic surfaces with Picard rank three.
2502.18894.methods: The authors construct Bridgeland stability conditions and analyze the walls in the stability manifold using the geometry of exceptional collections and the properties of the Mukai pairing.
2502.18894.regime: The results apply to the category of coherent sheaves on del Pezzo surfaces of degree six, which have Picard rank three.
2502.18894.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques developed for analyzing stability walls on Picard rank three surfaces may generalize to higher-rank Fano varieties and more general systematically constructed exceptional collections.

2502.19223.problem: The paper establishes the triviality of the kernel of the natural map on Galois cohomology sets of reductive groups over certain localized rings, thereby proving cases of the Nisnevich conjecture.
2502.19223.methods: The proof utilizes patching diagrams for torsors, the Serre-Grothendieck conjecture for semilocal Dedekind rings, and the structure of strictly proper parabolic subgroups of reductive group schemes.
2502.19223.regime: The results apply to strictly isotropic simply connected reductive groups over Dedekind domains and regular local rings of dimensions two and three.
2502.19223.hyporhesized_generalization: The results hint at a general positive resolution of the Nisnevich conjecture for strictly isotropic reductive groups over arbitrary regular local rings.

2502.19018.problem: The paper solves the problem of finding explicit algebraic equations and fields of definition for a surface and its minimal-entropy automorphism, which were previously only known to exist abstractly through transcendental and Hodge-theoretic methods.
2502.19018.methods: The authors construct the explicit equations by identifying a K3 surface with a matching transcendental lattice, computing its Weierstrass model via an elliptic fibration, and representing the automorphism through its lift to the universal cover.
2502.19018.regime: The results apply to complex algebraic surfaces, specifically Enriques and K3 surfaces, and extend to positive characteristic fields via reduction modulo prime numbers.
2502.19018.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint that the minimal entropy of automorphisms on Enriques surfaces in characteristic zero may also serve as the minimum entropy bound for Enriques surfaces in positive characteristic.

2502.19266.problem: The paper aims to characterize the codimension and algebraic invariants of intersections and unions of matrix Schubert varieties using a combinatorial order structure on alternating sign matrices.
2502.19266.methods: The authors apply weak Bruhat order operators, K-theoretic divided difference operators, and derivative formulas to analyze the geometric properties of alternating sign matrix varieties.
2502.19266.regime: The results apply to finite-dimensional matrix Schubert varieties and their arbitrary unions and intersections indexed by alternating sign matrices.
2502.19266.hypothesized_generalization: The algebraic and combinatorial properties established for weak order on alternating sign matrices may generalize to provide a unified framework for computing multidegrees and Schubert structure constants for arbitrary unions of matrix Schubert varieties.

2502.19296.problem: The paper aims to determine whether the equivariant Kuznetsov component of a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution is equivalent to the derived category of a surface.
2502.19296.methods: The authors construct a Fourier-Mukai functor between derived categories, prove its fully faithful property using Bondal-Orlov criteria, and establish the equivalence by comparing semi-orthogonal decompositions of equivariant blow-ups and root stacks.
2502.19296.regime: The results apply to general cubic fourfolds admitting a symplectic involution, where the fixed locus of the involution is non-equidimensional.
2502.19296.hypothesized_generalization: The result suggests that the equivariant Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds with symplectic automorphisms can be systematically described by the derived categories of associated surfaces, extending the Beckmann-Oberdieck result to non-commutative settings.

2502.19403.problem: How to construct a robust homotopical framework for non-commutative derived analytic moduli functors that reconciles topological algebra structures with algebraic functional calculus.
2502.19403.methods: We develop a formulation of free entire functional calculus (FEFC) on differential graded algebras and establish equivalence results with topological dg algebras by formally inverting abstract homology isomorphisms.
2502.19403.regime: The setting of non-commutative derived analytic geometry, specifically operating on pro-Banach, nuclear Fréchet, and finitely generated topological dg algebras.
2502.19403.hypothesized_generalization: The framework suggests that many analytic moduli functors of algebraic origin can be systematically studied as homotopy limits of algebraic functors evaluated on complete tensor products with nuclear Fréchet algebras.

2502.19408.problem: The paper resolves the discrepancy between different enumerative invariants at higher genus by establishing a precise correspondence between quantum periods of mirror curves and all-genus logarithmic two-point invariants.
2502.19408.methods: The authors employ the topological vertex formalism, tropical correspondence for refined descendant invariants, and combinatorial Laurent series methods including a q-refined Lagrange inversion formula.
2502.19408.regime: The results apply to smooth log Calabi-Yau pairs, specifically smooth projective Fano surfaces with a smooth anticanonical divisor, at arbitrary genus and winding.
2502.19408.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint at a broader correspondence where quantum periods of mirror curves systematically encode the all-genus open and closed Gromov-Witten theory for higher-dimensional toric Calabi-Yau manifolds.

2502.19445.problem: The paper aims to establish a precise algebraic correspondence between the cohomological Hall algebras of one-dimensional sheaves on surfaces and the positive halves of affine Yangians of corresponding Lie algebras.
2502.19445.methods: The authors employ a continuity theorem for t-structures on derived categories and analyze the action of the braid group on preprojective algebras of quivers to prove a PBW-type theorem.
2502.19445.regime: The results apply to Kleinian resolutions of singularities and elliptic surfaces of types D and E.
2502.19445.hypothesized_generalization: The authors conjecture a general PBW-type theorem relating the cohomological Hall algebras of pairs of curves on a surface when their intersection is zero-dimensional.

2502.19598.problem: Determine the conditions under which a group action on a variety is equivariantly unirational or stably linearizable, specifically focusing on the necessity and sufficiency of having fixed points under all abelian subgroups.
2502.19598.methods: Analyzing the equivariant birational geometry of Fano threefolds of index two by translating group actions into twists over nonclosed fields via torsors.
2502.19598.regime: Generically free actions of finite groups on smooth and singular Fano threefolds of index two over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
2502.19598.thought_process: The paper hints that the equivalence between the existence of abelian fixed points and equivariant unirationality, established here for certain Fano threefolds, may extend to other classes of higher-dimensional geometrically rational varieties.

2502.19600.problem: The paper investigates the geometric and algebraic intersections of correspondences on modular curves to determine their intersection numbers and algebraic properties.
2502.19600.methods: The authors employ intersection theory, the geometry of modular curves, and the algebraic properties of Hecke operators acting on divisor classes.
2502.19600.regime: The results apply to classical modular curves of arbitrary level and their associated Hecke correspondences over the complex numbers.
2502.19600.hypothesized_generalization: The intersection formulas may generalize to higher-dimensional Shimura varieties and more general arithmetic intersection theory settings.

2502.19626.problem: The paper addresses the problem of establishing the existence, uniqueness, and compactification-independence of functorial weight filtrations on cohomology theories evaluated on non-proper or singular objects.
2502.19626.methods: The authors construct the weight filtration as an exact functor taking values in filtered spectra by extending the Postnikov filtration from the subcategory of pure motives to the subcategory of resolvable motives within the stable infinity-category of modules over a motivic spectrum.
2502.19626.regime: The results apply to any representable, linear cohomology theory on smooth schemes over an affine Dedekind base scheme, evaluated on motives that can be resolved by smooth projective schemes.
2502.19626.hyporhesized_generalization: The authors expect that the abstractly constructed weight filtration on colocalized cohomology theories coincides with the classical weight filtrations traditionally defined on logarithmic crystalline and de Rham cohomology groups over more general bases.

2502.19703.problem: The paper investigates the geometric singularities and algebraic relations defining the higher-order secant constructions of smooth projective manifolds.
2502.19703.methods: The authors analyze the syzygies and singularity types by studying the behavior of vector bundles and resolution of singularities on the symmetric products of algebraic varieties.
2502.19703.regime: The results apply to smooth projective varieties of arbitrary dimension embedded via sufficiently ample line bundles.
2502.19703.hypothesized_generalization: The techniques suggest a general framework for characterizing the defining equations and singularities of secant varieties for a broader class of singular or singular-like projective schemes.

2502.19910.problem: The paper establishes a duality theorem for the Weil-étale realization of 1-motives defined over non-archimedean local fields.
2502.19910.methods: The approach utilizes condensed mathematics and the formalism of Weil-Deligne groups to analyze the cohomology of 1-motives.
2502.19910.regime: The results apply to 1-motives over p-adic fields within the framework of condensed abelian groups.
2502.19910.hypothesized_generalization: The duality framework may generalize to higher-dimensional motives or more general schemes over local fields.

2502.19988.problem: Formulating and analyzing a local-global principle for the algebraicity of leaves in geometric foliations and their associated loci of special structures.
2502.19988.methods: Analyzing the Taylor series of periods, module structures of differential forms, and reduction modulo prime ideals of linear differential equations and vector fields.
2502.19988.regime: Foliations and leaf schemes defined over finitely generated subrings of the complex numbers.
2502.19988.hypothesized_generalization: A unified local-global framework linking the algebraicity of Hodge loci to the modulo-prime behavior of associated differential systems, potentially refining the Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture.

2502.20094.problem: The paper characterizes the geometric structure and singular behavior of the exceptional locus arising from the resolution of singularities on moduli spaces of sheaves.
2502.20094.methods: The authors employ birational geometry and deformation theory to analyze the exceptional divisors of symplectic resolutions of singular moduli spaces.
2502.20094.regime: The results apply to higher-dimensional generalized Kummer varieties and O'Grady-type moduli spaces of stable sheaves on K3 or abelian surfaces.
2502.20094.hypothesized_generalization: The structural description of the exceptional locus suggests a general framework for describing the intersection cohomology and birational models of other singular symplectic varieties.

2502.20515.problem: The lack of a framework to define enumerative invariants for moduli stacks of objects that lie outside of Calabi-Yau abelian categories or linear structures.
2502.20515.methods: Constructing stability measures and epsilon motives on the component lattice of a 1-shifted symplectic derived Artin stack.
2502.20515.regime: Derived Artin stacks of finite presentation over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
2502.20515.hypothesized_generalization: A unified, category-free framework for enumerative geometry and wall-crossing phenomena across general algebraic stacks.

2502.20327.problem: The paper aims to compute the intersection cohomology of singular moduli spaces of semistable vector bundles on Riemann surfaces in the case of non-coprime rank and degree.
2502.20327.methods: The authors apply the Decomposition Theorem to a forgetful projection map from a smooth parabolic moduli space to the singular moduli space, analyzing the cohomology of the fibers and the resulting local systems.
2502.20327.regime: The result applies to moduli spaces of semistable vector bundles of arbitrary rank and degree zero over smooth complex projective curves of any genus.
2502.20327.hypothesized_generalization: The geometric methods and the Decomposition Theorem framework used here could potentially be generalized to compute the intersection cohomology of other singular moduli spaces of sheaves or Higgs bundles on curves.

2502.20761.problem: The paper addresses the problem of determining whether certain algebraic varieties are stably rational, which means they are birationally equivalent to projective space after taking a product with a projective space.
2502.20761.methods: The authors use the specialization method, refined by Schreieder, to compute relative unramified cohomology groups of fibrations in del Pezzo surfaces of degree 2.
2502.20761.regime: The results apply to double covers of products of projective lines branched along very general divisors of specific bidegrees over uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic not equal to 2.
2502.20761.hypothesized_generalization: The results hint at a broader principle that specific geometric constructions of reference varieties, combined with the specialization method, can effectively determine stable rationality for various classes of algebraic varieties.

2502.20544.problem: The paper addresses the characterization of fundamental algebraic sets within the context of locally unit-additive rings.
2502.20544.methods: The paper employs techniques from algebraic geometry and commutative algebra to analyze the properties of these ring structures and their associated sets.
2502.20544.regime: The results apply to algebraic structures where the concept of unit-additivity is locally defined, providing insights into their geometric properties.
2502.20544.hypothesized_generalization: The findings suggest a deeper connection between the algebraic properties of rings and the geometric characteristics of their associated sets, potentially generalizable to broader classes of non-commutative or non-associative algebras.

2502.20618.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of defining and computing Chow groups with twisted coefficients, generalizing existing definitions to a broader class of coefficient sheaves.
2502.20618.methods: The authors define twisted Chow groups using the cokernel of a residue map on Galois cohomology groups, operating on locally constant étale sheaves of abelian groups.
2502.20618.regime: The results apply to separated schemes of finite type over a field, with coefficients in locally constant étale sheaves, including both torsion and non-torsion cases.
2502.20618.hypothesized_generalization: The work conjectures a definition of Chow groups twisted by any birational sheaf with transfers, suggesting a broader framework for twisted Chow groups.
